IIT Mandi Catalyst, in collaboration with Startup Himachal and HPCED (Department of Industries, Government of Himachal Pradesh), successfully conducted a workshop at Govt. ITI Bagsaid, Mandi, under the RAMP Programme.

Led by Minni Kaur, Senior Associate, IIT Mandi Catalyst, the session focused on rural entrepreneurship, pre-incubation, and early-stage innovation, covering key areas such as:
🔹 Benefits of the RAMP Programme for the institute and students
🔹 Identifying local problems and exploring opportunities to address them
🔹 Understanding local resources and income-generation opportunities and learning how to scale them into sustainable ventures

A highlight of the session was an SHG showcasing its products, including flower garlands and handmade Himachali “Poolen,” demonstrating how local skills, traditional crafts, and community resources can be transformed into entrepreneurial opportunities.

The session aimed to empower students and aspiring entrepreneurs to identify local challenges, leverage available resources, and transform ideas and skills into viable ventures.

Special thanks to the management and faculty of Govt. ITI Bagsaid, Mandi, for their support in strengthening the rural innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem.

Researchers at IIT Delhi have developed a scalable, atomically thin 𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗶-𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵 𝗰𝗼𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗴𝗹𝗮𝘀𝘀 that improves scratch resistance without hindering the optical transparency of the glass.

The work was conducted under the guidance of 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗳. Nitya Nand Gosvami and 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗳. N M Anoop Krishnan 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗜𝗜𝗧 𝗗𝗲𝗹𝗵𝗶, along with 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗳. Viswanath Balakrishnan 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗜𝗜𝗧 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗶.

A two-dimensional tungsten disulfide (WS₂) film is coated directly on the glass surface in a single-step chemical vapour deposition process. 

𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘂𝗹𝘁𝘀:
 • Nanoscale friction reduced by ~95% against a diamond probe (AFM scratch testing)
 • Severe plowing wear suppressed, even with a single monolayer
 • Uniform growth demonstrated over 0.25 m²
 
With applications spanning electronics, architectural glazing, automotive glazing and aerospace glass, this technology opens new possibilities for improving the durability of glass surfaces without compromising their optical performance.

His vision is to build at the intersection of 𝐤𝐧𝐨𝐰𝐥𝐞𝐝𝐠𝐞, 𝐢𝐧𝐧𝐨𝐯𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐞𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐮𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩, helping students discover entrepreneurship, researchers take ideas beyond the lab, founders access the right ecosystem, and industry discover new possibilities within the university.

It’s about bringing together people, ideas and opportunities that might otherwise never meet.

From 𝐀𝐡𝐦𝐞𝐝𝐚𝐛𝐚𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐆𝐮𝐣𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐭, 𝐆𝐮𝐣𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐨 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐚, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐚 𝐭𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝, there is a lot to build.

And that is exactly what makes it exciting.

𝐖𝐞𝐥𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐕𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐒𝐭𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐨, 𝐑𝐚𝐠𝐡𝐮𝐯𝐞𝐞𝐫. 🚀

A meaningful exchange between two innovation ecosystems. 🇮🇳🇯🇵

We were delighted to welcome Hisashi Nakazawa, Director, Kobe Trade Information Office in Singapore, Kobe City Government, to VentureStudio, Ahmedabad University.

The visit offered an opportunity to explore how we support innovation from research and prototyping to incubation and commercialization, particularly across healthcare, life sciences and deep-tech.

During the visit, Mr. Nakazawa toured our three facilities and got a closer look at the infrastructure and capabilities available to innovators. He also interacted with our startups, gaining firsthand insights into the problems they are solving, their journeys, and the process of building and scaling from an academic ecosystem.

With Kobe’s strong biomedical, medical-device and biomanufacturing ecosystem, and Ahmedabad’s growing innovation and entrepreneurship landscape, there is significant potential for knowledge exchange, cross-border collaboration and stronger bridges between our two ecosystems.

Thank you, Mr. Nakazawa, for spending time with us and for the engaging conversations. We look forward to exploring what we can build together.
